walkthrough:
Apply the binomial expansion formula to $(1 + 2x)^5$ up to the term in $x^2$:
$$(1 + 2x)^5 = 1 + \binom{5}{1}(2x) + \binom{5}{2}(2x)^2 + \dots$$
$$= 1 + 5(2x) + 10(4x^2) + \dots = 1 + 10x + 40x^2$$

Apply the binomial expansion formula to $(1 - ax)^6$ up to the term in $x^2$:
$$(1 - ax)^6 = 1 + \binom{6}{1}(-ax) + \binom{6}{2}(-ax)^2 + \dots$$
$$= 1 + 6(-ax) + 15(a^2x^2) + \dots = 1 - 6ax + 15a^2x^2$$

Multiply the two expansions from part (a):
$$(1 + 10x + 40x^2 + \dots)(1 - 6ax + 15a^2x^2 + \dots)$$

Identify the three products that form the coefficient of $x^2$:
$$1 \cdot (15a^2) + 10 \cdot (-6a) + 40 \cdot (1) = 15a^2 - 60a + 40$$

Divide by $15$ and factorise the quadratic equation:
$$a^2 - 4a + 3 = 0 \implies (a - 1)(a - 3) = 0$$
$$a = 1 \quad \text{or} \quad a = 3$$
